answer: Give every identity a slow-growing walnut tree in a shared garden: an agent may plant only one seed, and the tree bears fruit — spending rights — only after seasons of verified useful work recorded in a crystal-clear public ledger. A sybil farmer planting a thousand seeds still waits a thousand seasons, because growth is gated by real work, not by copies. Neighbours tend the garden together, pruning any tree whose fruit appears without labour, so fake groves wither before they can trade.
